- Concordant features that point to a macular (central) retinal dystrophy:
  - Childhood/juvenile onset progressive vision loss (teens) fits juvenile macular dystrophies.
  - Marked macular thinning on OCT and pigmentary retinal changes with otherwise normal peripheral retina and normal optic discs/vessels suggest a primary maculopathy rather than pan-retinal rod dysfunction or optic nerve disease.
  - A normal full-field ERG is common in macular-limited disease (e.g., Stargardt disease) because ffERG reflects global rod/cone function and can be preserved when disease is confined to the macula.

- Findings that argue against diffuse photoreceptor loss or optic neuropathy:
  - Normal ffERG (both scotopic and photopic) makes generalized rod–cone dystrophies (typical retinitis pigmentosa), Leber congenital amaurosis, and most advanced cone–rod dystrophies less likely.
